newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark stretches resistance, 1.60 calls.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark stretches resistance, 1.60 calls.

text.p: Monday's 29-month dollar/mark high of 1.5925 slightly surpassed several major trendlines intersecting near 1.59, according to chartists.
But resistance near 1.59 marks may only briefly deflect the greenback's long-term rally, and the dollar could soon test the looming 1.6050 target, they said.
The dollar hopped above 1.5890 marks, where channel resistance dating back to April 1995 joins a rising trendline from September 1995, chartists said.
Randolph Donney, director of capital markets at Pegasus Econometric Group, said, "If we push clearly through that barrier on a closing basis, we may waltz straight up to 1.60."
The 1.6050-marks area represents a nearly irresistible attraction, with several important technical studies and long-term trends all pointing there, chartists said.

In addition to being the 62-percent retracement of the dollar's decline from 1.7680 in February 1994 to 1.3430 in March 1995, 1.6050 marks is distinguished by correspoinding to the major downtrend line off the June 1989 high of 2.0480, they said.
"That is a trendline which comes in -- boom -- right on the same place," said Scott Siller, senior techinal analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch. "They are both lining up right there."

Siller said there was a high risk of major profit taking on the dollar's rally at that point. But, he said his daily and weekly oscillators were making new highs, showing no signs of bearish divergence with prices.

Intermediate resistance for the dollar lies at 1.5950/75 marks, they said. Any backsliding for the dollar is likely to be check at 1.5835, with the base of the dollar's current seven day trendline at 1.5810 seen as the short term bottom.
Meanwhile, dollar/yen continues to consolidate for the time being, but technicians said it would eventually move above 117 with an objective of 118.25.
"It is still milling about in a trading range between 115 and 117," Donney said. It looks like we'll get another attempt at the upside in the next couple of days."
On Monday, the dollar closed at 1.5884/89 marks, up from 1.5871/76 marks at the U.S. open. It finished at 116.45/50 yen, up from 116.33/38 yen.
